ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The image shows structural formulas labeled Methanol, Propane, Ethene, and Ethanal. The relevant compounds are propane, shown as a three-carbon hydrocarbon with single bonds and formula C3H8, and ethene, shown as a two-carbon hydrocarbon with a C=C double bond and formula C2H4. Reasoning: Propane and ethene are both nonpolar hydrocarbons, so hydrogen bonding and strong dipole-dipole interactions are not the main comparison. The main intermolecular force is London dispersion. Propane is larger and has more electrons than ethene, so its electron cloud is more polarizable. More polarizable molecules have stronger London dispersion forces, requiring more energy to separate them in boiling. Therefore, propane will likely have the higher boiling point.
